one_month_reasoning: The window (to 2026-11-04) contains Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-29 (Yahoo calendar, not flagged as an estimate). Guide is $860-870M revenue / $385-395M adj EBITDA; consensus $872M sits at the top of the guide, and Reddit beat the top of its guide by ~10-11% in Q1 and Q2 2026, so a revenue print near $930-950M is likely. But the stock has reacted to users, not revenue: after the Q2'26 print (61% growth, big beat) it fell 21% the next day (178.04 to 140.67) on a sequential US DAU decline; Q4'25 -7%, Q3'25 +7%. From Q3 the company stops reporting the logged-in/logged-out split, which removes one bear datapoint but may be read as hiding weakness; Google licence renewal news could also land. A likely revenue beat is offset by user/search risk, so I see no clear direction: median at today's price, log-sd ~19% (about the 20% annual-vol/3.5 base, since the ~12-15% typical earnings move dominates the month), slightly fat tails.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The premium rests on structural differences that should persist through Oct-2027: (1) revenue growth ~27% in CY27 vs peer median ~13%, with global ARPU only $6.18 vs US $11.85, so monetisation headroom is measurable rather than asserted; (2) adj EBITDA margin already ~45% with capex ~0.1% of revenue (FCF near EBITDA), better than every peer except APP; (3) $2.8B net cash, ~zero debt. Offsetting: dependence on Google search referrals and a falling US DAU base, which is why I stay well below SPOT/SNAP and well under a growth-parity multiple. Basis caveat: all peer EPS are Yahoo consensus CY2027 averages from one source (each contributor's own GAAP/adjusted basis); EV/EBITDA is a rough proxy = current EV / (TTM GAAP EBITDA x CY27/CY26 revenue growth), so it overstates SBC-heavy names (PINS, DUOL, SPOT).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$105 (about 18x my CY27 taxed EPS, ~12x CY27 adj EBITDA net of cash, well below the 52-week low of $119.27) the market would be pricing growth falling to peer levels, which would most likely mean a fundamental break: a sustained US DAU decline that ad pricing cannot offset, loss of the Google relationship (licence and traffic), or a guide-down, rather than ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Primary documents show an exceptional business on financial metrics: revenue +61% in Q2'26 to $805M, adj EBITDA margin 43% (Q3 guide 45%), FCF roughly equal to OCF with capex ~$1M/qtr, $2.8B cash, 207M diluted shares, $760M buyback left, SBC guided down to low-to-mid-teens % of revenue. Reddit beat the top of its revenue guide by ~10% in Q1 and Q2 2026, so 2026 is tracking ~$3.55B vs consensus $3.39B. The bear case is about users, not money: US DAUq growth slowed 9% -> 7% -> 6% with a sequential decline in Q2; management calls search referral visibility 'low' and will stop disclosing the logged-in split; the 10-Q RPO shows only $30.1M of licensing revenue contracted for 2027 while the ~$60M Google deal is in contentious renewal. The stock fell 21% on the Q2 print despite the beat and is -27% over the year. The 10-Q also flags a likely valuation-allowance release, so 2027 EPS should carry a ~22% tax rate; taxing the street's view gives ~$5.90, putting the stock at ~26x taxed CY27 EPS vs a peer median of 19x (10 calendar-2027 peers, one consensus source). Fair value $200 (25x CY28 taxed EPS = $193; 4% SBC-adjusted FCF yield = $208). I don't use the full fair value as the median because user/traffic risk is fat-tailed: scenarios $95 (28%) / $180 (47%) / $275 (25%), mean ~$180, median ~$165. The ladder is a lognormal around ~$163 with sigma ~0.6 (below 70% realised vol, which includes earnings-day gaps, but still very wide), checked against the scenario weights (P<$106 ~24% vs bear weight 28%). Research was limited to ~15 queries; Twelve Data estimate endpoints were unavailable on the current plan; no option data used.
